channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Huang Affair Suggests 'Compromised Objectivity' Says Anna Ashton
item.description: Anna Ashton, founder of Ashton Analytics and former China analyst at the Department of Defense, said that it doesn't matter if Alice Huang was an unwitting participant or a spy for the Chinese government because she already worked for Megaspeed, a company that was 'seriously distrusted' for attempting to work around US export controls on chips. Ashton said that Jensen Huang's affair with Alice Huang suggests 'massively compromised objectivity' on the part of the former Nvidia CEO. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia’s $10B Anthropic IPO Pledge in Focus With CEO Exit
item.description: Bloomberg Intelligence’s Mandeep Singh and Bloomberg’s Anthony Hughes joins Scarlet Fu on “Bloomberg Real Yield.” Anthropic’s plans for a record initial public offering are under fresh scrutiny after Nvidia’s CEO was unexpectedly ousted, highlighting the links between the two artificial intelligence giants. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI ‘Supply Shock’ Pushes Bond Market to Limit, Wells Fargo Says
item.description: Technology giants racing to build artificial intelligence infrastructure are hitting the limit of how much they can raise in global bond markets, according to Wells Fargo & Co.
item.dc:creator: Scarlet Fu and Michelle Cheng

item.title: How Huang’s Resignation Could Hurt US AI
item.description: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had direct access to President Donald Trump and more influence over American AI policy than any other Silicon Valley executive. Bloomberg Opinion columnist Dave Lee explains the risks to the sector without its leather-jacketed champion. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Internet Brands Eyes $3.5 Billion Debt Sale for Refinancing
item.description: KKR & Co.-backed Internet Brands is testing investor appetite for a roughly $3.5 billion debt package to refinance its existing loans, as concerns about artificial intelligence disruption weigh on sentiment toward software businesses.
item.dc:creator: Gowri Gurumurthy, Paula Seligson and Michelle Cheng

item.title: AI ‘Supply Shock’ Pushes Bond Market to Limit: O’Connor
item.description: Maureen O’Connor, global head of high-grade debt syndicate at Wells Fargo, joins Scarlet Fu on “Bloomberg Real Yield.” They discuss the record amount of issuance in the US high-grade market this year. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple’s Former Chief Chip Architect on Working With Srouji
item.description: On this episode of the Power On podcast, Nuvacore Co-Founder Gerard Williams III talks to Mark Gurman about his time at Apple as chief CPU architect and what it was like working alongside chief hardware officer Johny Srouji to develop the company’s groundbreaking A7 and M1 processors. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Govt. Action Around Huang Affair Reveals Lack of Guardrails, Says Rep. Dexter
item.description: Democratic Representative Maxine Dexter talked about her bill to ban new data centers on federal public lands and the potential national security risks posed by the Nvidia scandal. Dexter said that the government inaction around Huang's affair reveals a lack of guardrails and regulations around national security. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Microsoft Says It’s Working to Fix Outlook, Copilot Outage
item.description: Microsoft Corp. said it was working to restore access to its bundle of workplace software, saying customers may experience issues connecting to email and other tools.
item.dc:creator: Matt Day

item.title: ‘Dark Day’: Silicon Valley Mourns Nvidia’s Decision to Oust CEO
item.description: The ouster of Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang has sent shockwaves throughout Silicon Valley, prompting a chorus of venture capitalists and founders to criticize the chipmaker’s decision and express concerns about the broader impact on the industry. Huang was removed by Nvidia’s board of directors after reports of two affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China and another with an employee. Huang, the only CEO in Nvidia’s three-decade history, will no longe
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Torrence

item.title: Twitch CEO: GTA VI Could Be Our Biggest Moment
item.description: Twitch CEO Dan Clancy sat down with Bloomberg’s Romaine Bostick from his company’s annual “TwitchCon” to discuss the rise of the creator economy in streaming, and how Twitch is preparing for the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia Names Colette Kress as Interim CEO
item.description:
Nvidia turns to CFO Colette Kress to steady the ship as interim CEO, following Jensen Huang’s ouster.
Norah Mulinda explains. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia CEO Ouster Shakes AI Economy
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Nvidia loses the man who built its AI empire. Jensen Huang is out after a stunning boardroom shakeup, wiping hundreds of billions from Nvidia’s value and rattling the entire AI trade. We break down what comes next for the AI industry and how it’s playing out in Washington and on Wall Street. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Jensen Huang Ousted By Nvidia Board As CEO
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down the news of Jensen Huang ousted from his post as Nvidia CEO after reports of two affairs, including one with a woman US officials reportedly suspected of spying for China. Now investors are confronting a question that barely existed days ago: what is Nvidia without Jensen Huang? (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Former Prosecutor Breaks Down Nvidia’s Legal Exposure
item.description: Questions remain over the potential legal and national security fallout for Nvidia and former CEO Jensen Huang following revelations about Huang’s relationship with a woman alleged to have ties to Chinese intelligence. Miller & Chevalier partner and former federal prosecutor Christina Clark explains how counterintelligence and criminal investigations could proceed in parallel and why Nvidia’s independent board investigation may represent only one piece of a broader government inquiry. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Probes If Alice Huang Helped Smuggle Super Micro Products
item.description: The Justice Department is probing Alice Huang, the woman US officials suspect as a possible spy targeting the ousted head of Nvidia Corp., over whether entities linked to her were involved in efforts to smuggle products made by Super Micro Computer Inc. to China, according to a person familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Chris Strohm

item.title: Nvidia’s Huang Ousted by Board in Move That Roils AI Economy
item.description: Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang, the preeminent face of the AI infrastructure boom, was ousted from his post after reports of three affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China.
item.dc:creator: Ian King

item.title: Nvidia Default-Risk Gauge Improves Following CEO Huang’s Ouster
item.description: The cost of protecting Nvidia Corp.’s debt against default declined on Thursday, after Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang was ousted from his post amid reports of two affairs.
item.dc:creator: Caleb Mutua

item.title: Cinco gráficos que muestran la enorme relevancia de Nvidia
item.description: Nvidia llegó a acercarse a una valoración de US$6 billones. Ahora, el escándalo de Jensen Huang ha golpeado sus acciones y expuesto un problema que inquieta a los inversionistas: no hay un sucesor claro.
item.dc:creator: Tom Pfeiffer, Ingrid Fuary-Wagner and Wendy Pollack

item.title: Everybody Will Be Hacked At Some Point: Ledger CEO
item.description: Pascal Gauthier, chairman and CEO of Ledger, joins Isabelle Lee and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." The hackers who stole $6.3 billion from Binance last week found a way to take 40% of the stolen cryptocurrency in one hit, reducing their chances of being caught in the act, and it cost them just $15. (Source: Bloomberg)
